Faux Cyrillic Text Generator

Cyrillic letters standing in for Latin ones, and not a word of Russian

Symbol Alphabets
  • Faux Cyrillic
  • Greek Style
  • Currency / Crossed
  • All 32 styles →

It looks Russian. It is not Russian.

Д is not an A, И is not an N, and Я is not an R. What this style does is pick Cyrillic letters that resemble Latin shapes and stand them in, a swap of characters rather than a change of font, and the same trick paperback covers and film posters have leaned on for decades. Д is a d sound, И is an i, Я is closer to ya. It reads as Russian only to people who do not read Russian.

Letters with no believable stand-in are left as Latin, so the effect is patchy by design, and the set carries no digits at all. That patchiness is arguably the honest part, since the style has always been a costume rather than a translation. It works on cover art, a band name or a clan tag where the reference is the whole point, and it works badly anywhere a reader might take you to be writing in the language.

Also searched as: russian style text, fake russian font, cyrillic looking letters.

Where Faux Cyrillic text works, and where it does not

WorksReads as ordinary text everywhere, because these are normal Unicode letters rather than a maths alphabet. Watch outUnicode has no character for every letter in this style, so the missing ones stay plain. That is the honest fallback, not a fault.

Faux Cyrillic questions

Is this actual Russian?

Not remotely. The letters are genuine Cyrillic, but they were chosen purely for resembling Latin shapes, so the result spells nothing in any language that uses the alphabet. Д is a d sound, И is an i, Я is closer to ya. A Russian reader sees a string of unrelated consonants and vowels.

Why did some of my letters not change?

Because no convincing lookalike exists for them. Cyrillic and Latin share ancestry in places and diverge completely in others, so several letters have nothing to stand in. Rather than blank them out or force a poor match that breaks the illusion, this generator leaves those letters exactly as you typed them.

What is it actually good for?

Cover art, band names, a poster pastiche, a joke about a cold war thriller. It carries one very specific visual reference and almost nothing else, which is fine when that reference is what you want. Bear in mind that mixing scripts can trip filters on services watching for lookalike impersonation.
